title_eng: Feasibility Study of Respiration Monitoring based on Strip-Type Force Sensing Platform in Various Lying Positions

feasibility of respiration monitoring based on strip -type force 
sensing platform in various lying positions. Respiratory 
component was recorded in four lying position s (supine, left 
lateral, right lateral and prone ) and frequency component s of 
the signal, kurtosis of reference respiration frequency and total 
frequency power, were compared statistically. The r esult 
showed that respiratory component is well re flected in every 
lying position and is strongly observed in prone position.

Unconstrained sensing technology is advantageous for 
long-term and continuous monitoring of physiological signals, 
which recently have been actively developed for sleep 
environment. One of representative examples is the strip-type 
sensing platform for monitoring of respiration and heart beat 
[1, 2]. In our research, we aim to validate the feasibility of 
strip-type force sensing platform according to various lying 
positions as an unconstrained respiration monitoring system.

showed that respiratory component is well re flected in every 
lying position and is strongly observed in prone position. 
I. INTRODUCTION 
Unconstrained sensing technology is advantageous for 
long-term and continuous monitoring of physiological signals, 
which recently have been actively developed for sleep 
environment. One of representative examples is the strip-type 
sensing platform for monitoring of respiration and heart beat 
[1, 2]. In our research, we aim to validate the feasibility of 
strip-type force sensing platform according to various lying 
positions as an unconstrained respiration monitoring system. 
II. MATERIALS AND METHOD 
Strip-type force sensing platform consists of the 
piezo-resistive strip force sensor, FSR -408 (Interlink 
Electronics, CA, USA) and ultra-low power microcontroller, 
MSP430 (Texas Instruments, TX, USA). Dimension of sensor 
part is 65.5×2.5 cm (length×width). An e xperiment was 
conducted with ten participants (5 males and 5 females , 
169.6±6.1 cm, 71.9±20.8 kg, 21.7±3.0 years old) in four lying 
positions; supine, right lateral, left lateral and prone. To record 
the respiratory movement, s ensor module was located 
underneath of subjects’ chest. During the experiment, subjects 
were requested to breathe with metronome’s beep sound (0.25 
Hz). Signals were recorded for 150 seconds with 50 Hz 
sampling frequency by each position. 
To evaluate whether the lying position has an effect on 
respiration component recorded by strip-type force sensor, we 
compared the kurtosis and the frequency power of obtained 
signals in each position. Before an analysis, in pre-processing 
stage, we removed the baseline of signal , then extracted the 
frequency component of respiration based on 5 th order 
auto-regressive model after band pass filtering (passband: 0.15 
to 0.4 Hz). Kurtosis and frequency power were calculated in 
the frequency range 0.125 to 0.375 Hz around reference 
respiration rate (0.25 Hz) . Every procedure of signal 
processing was conducted using Matlab 2015b (Mathworks, 
MA, USA), and SPSS Statistics v ersion 23 (IBM, IL, USA) 
was used for statistical validation. 
III. RESULT AND DISCUSSION 
As a result, significant positive kurtosis ( 4.38±1.88) was 
observed in every lying position (see Fig. 1(a)). This is a 
‘heavy tailed distribution’ around the reference respiration 
rate, which indicates a respiratory component is strongly 
reflected. Statistically, significant difference between lying 
positions was not found in kurtosis (Friedman test, p>0.05) but 
was found in total power (Friedman test, p<0.05). Therefore, 
to investigate the lying position -induced difference, we 
conducted additional analysis based on Wilcoxon test and 
Bonferroni correction. The result showed that the significance 
difference (p<0.0083) was found in prone position compared 
with other positions (see Fig. 1(b)). In the prone position, total 
power is much greater (673.5 to 865.8%) than other positions. 
IV. CONCLUSION 
In this research, we evaluated the feasibility of respiration 
monitoring according to the lying positions based on 
strip-type force sensing system . Our result show ed that the 
strip-type sensing system has the possibility of respiration 
monitoring in various lying positions. Moreover, it also shown 
that respiratory component is strongly reflected in the prone 
position. For more practical validation, further studies 
including clinical setting like polysomnography are needed in 
the actual sleep situation.
